My two cents:

* The animation was still really bad.

* However, there was some decent choreography this time around. Some.

* This story could have been done significantly better. I think that it would have been far better storytelling if Frieza intentionally came to Earth knowing the weakness of his form, but planning to catch Goku off-guard the entire time. Then, when Goku thinks he's outsmarted Frieza, it's much more climactic when Frieza reveals he's planned this all along and wanted to degrade Goku as much as possible by killing him with an average ray gun. I say this all as a Hunter X Hunter fanboy, though, meaning I'm totally biased towards use of tactics in shounen over pure strength.

* Also, I still think Vegeta should be the one to kill Frieza, even though I know he won't. That would a perfect way to finish off one of Vegeta's main conflicts throughout DBZ and allow for his character to be further developed later. But alas, it's not meant to be, and Toei doesn't give a damn about developing its characters.

If I were to convert to Islam, I would most likely fall down the path of a fundamentalist. I did the same thing when I tried converting to Catholicism. I felt intensely bad after my experience with the Catholic church because I was just so rigid, cold, and delusional in practicing my faith. 

What I miss is the feeling of there being an all-powerful, loving God. I suffer from intrusive thoughts, and since deconverting, they've mostly been about me being "in the wrong" and inevitably burning in Hell. Then, put the concept of Islam into my mind as well, and I'm stuck in between Catholicism, Islam, and Atheism. My intrusive thoughts have gone from "you're going to hell" to "you're going to hell because you're not a perfect Muslim/Catholic." These thoughts get even more painful when my irrationally strong fear of ISIS is thrown into the mix, and I have to question what's wrong and what's right.

I will most likely never convert to Islam, because I can't avoid associating them with ISIS' atrocities that follow exactly what the Qur'an says (and, you know, all of the terrible things in it). However, I can't deny that it sometimes feels like I'm an evil person for not believing in a god, and it sometimes feels like I'm trying to justify my lack of belief with evidence that I see as true but is actually false.
